correctness.rationale: The chartwise ideal (f,f_u,f_v) contains 1 exactly when the chart has no geometric singular point; retaining f is necessary in characteristic two. The smoothness predicate is invariant under invertible coordinate substitutions. For a smooth a and a b with b,a+b smooth, the four tests at h,h+a,h+b,h+a+b certify all remaining vectors and exclude dependent triples because the zero form is not smooth. Division by 168=7·6·4 counts subspaces once. An independently written Buchberger and integer Walsh implementation exhausted 32,767 nonzero forms via 279 orbits (78 smooth, 10,920 smooth vectors) and returned 4,760,477,568 ordered bases, hence 28,336,176 nets. Replay: branches/870df41c-087e-4f0a-80ca-b8ec083e5de5/independent_quartic_nets_check.py and independent_quartic_nets_result.json. This full run shares the Walsh strategy with the frozen proof; direct correlation was independently checked only at selected translations, not for a second whole census. Finally at a common rational base point the first jets of a three-space would lie in a two-dimensional fiber of cotangent directions, so a nonzero section would have zero first jet and be singular there. This proves rational, not geometric, base-point freeness.

Prior work gives existence and the maximal system dimension for these very parameters, and nearby records tabulate individual quartics, pencils, or a restricted plane-filling family. None of those inspected results gives or implies the all-smooth plane count. Neither existence, the dimension bound, the smooth-form and pencil counts, nor the elementary rational-jet consequence is credited as a new census result.

value.rationale: The census supplies the number of maximal-dimensional all-smooth families for quartics in the smallest field, rather than another existence example or a count of individual equations. It is a concrete incidence invariant of the smooth quartic locus and provides the exact fixed-coordinate total needed to benchmark a future orbit classification or compare line-to-plane extensions. The rational-base obstruction explains why these maximal families occupy a different part of the parameter space from plane-filling systems. No classification of geometric base schemes or net orbits is claimed.
